statement: Written before any model in study 2 was fitted. Study 1's results WERE known when this was written (its H1 failed), so study 2 uses genes study 1 never examined. H6 and H7 were chosen because published work suggests they are TabPFN's strengths (full predictive distributions; benefiting from similar context examples); that is stated here so the choice is visible.
target_rule: study 1's rule (5-50% of discovery lines below -0.5, mean > -0.8, ranked by SD), ranks 21+, excluding study 1's primary and secondary genes; first 20
data: as study 1: train pool = 24Q4 Avana discovery lines, test = 24Q4 holdout lines; lines without expression excluded (study 1 clarification 1); features = top-50 |r| expression genes on the context lines only

methods.ridge: as study 1; uncertainty = prediction + empirical quantiles of its 5-fold cross-validated residuals on the context lines
methods.random_forest: as study 1; uncertainty = prediction + empirical quantiles of its 5-fold cross-validated residuals on the context lines
methods.mean: context mean; uncertainty = empirical quantiles of the context labels (the no-features reference)

metrics.r: Pearson r, predicted vs measured, over the test lines (as study 1)
metrics.pinball: mean pinball (quantile) loss over the 19 quantile levels and the test lines; a proper scoring rule for predictive distributions (lower is better)
metrics.coverage80: share of test lines inside the 10%-90% predictive interval (descriptive)

experiments.A_curve: k in [16, 64] random discovery lines (3 repeats, seeds 0..2) and k = all discovery lines (1 run); test = all holdout lines
experiments.B_prospective: context = all 24Q4 lines; test = 26Q3 Cas12 lines first screened after 24Q4 (study 1's E3 construction), only targets with Avana-vs-Cas12 agreement r >= 0.5 on overlap lines
experiments.C_similar_examples: 50 holdout lines (fixed random sample, seed 0) per target. 'similar': for each test line, context = the 64 discovery lines whose expression profile (the 2000 most variable genes on discovery lines, z-scored with discovery mean and SD) correlates most with the test line's; one fit per test line. 'random': 64 random discovery lines (3 repeats). Features in both arms: top-50 selected on all discovery lines. r computed over the 50 lines. With 'similar' context, the mean method is k-nearest-neighbours.
experiments.D_shuffled_labels: control: k = 64 (seed 0) with the context labels randomly permuted (seed 0); every method should then score r near 0

hypotheses.H5 (primary; replication of study 1 H1): at k = 16 and 64, mean over targets of r(TabPFN) - r(baseline) > 0 for baseline = ridge and random forest; 4 comparisons, gene-level bootstrap 98.75% intervals (Bonferroni); each supported if its interval excludes 0 in TabPFN's favour.
hypotheses.H6 (primary; uncertainty): at k = 16 and 64, mean over targets of pinball(baseline) - pinball(TabPFN) > 0 for baseline = ridge and random forest with cross-validated residual intervals; 4 comparisons, 98.75% intervals; each supported if its interval excludes 0 in TabPFN's favour.
hypotheses.H6b (secondary): the same pinball comparison at k = all discovery lines and in the prospective test; 95% intervals.
hypotheses.H7 (secondary; similar examples): r(TabPFN, similar context) - r(TabPFN, random context) > 0 over targets; 95% interval. Reported alongside: similar-context TabPFN vs k-nearest-neighbours and vs similar-context ridge and random forest (descriptive).
hypotheses.controls: D: mean |r| below 0.1 for every method (descriptive check that the methods use the labels).

predictions.H5: Given study 1: TabPFN ahead of ridge at k = 16; no clear difference from random forest.
predictions.H6: TabPFN ahead of both baselines, most clearly at k = 16 (cross-validated residuals from 13 lines give crude intervals; skewed dependency distributions don't suit a constant-shape interval).
predictions.H6b: Smaller TabPFN advantage with all lines; uncertain under the distribution shift of the prospective test.

reporting: every hypothesis is reported whatever the outcome, in the notebook and README, beside study 1.
